Package sc.fiji.snt

Class PathNodeEditor

java.lang.Object
sc.fiji.snt.PathNodeEditor
public final class PathNodeEditor extends Object
Viewer-agnostic node-editing operations on a single Path: the logic behind the 'Edit Mode' commands of InteractiveTracerCanvas (delete, insert, move, lock, radius, tag, re-root, split, undo), but free of any canvas/ImagePlus dependency so that it can be driven by other front-ends (e.g., Bdv/Bvv).

This class lives in sc.fiji.snt because several of the Path/PathAndFillManager members it relies on are package-scoped. It is a front-end helper: it holds no GUI state beyond the (optional) dialogs it is explicitly handed. All coordinates are calibrated (world) coordinates, i.e., the same space as Path.getNode(int).

Every operation returns a PathNodeEditor.Result: callers are expected to display PathNodeEditor.Result.message() (if any) and, when PathNodeEditor.Result.pathsChanged() is true, re-sync any rendering of the Path Manager.

Author:
Tiago Ferreira

    • connectToSecondaryPath

      public PathNodeEditor.Result connectToSecondaryPath(GuiUtils gui, boolean showDialog)
      Connects the active node of the editing path to the active node of the secondary path (the one edited previously). By default the editing path becomes the child (branching from the secondary path), but a heuristic and the user may swap roles. Asks for confirmation (the operation cannot be undone). On success the editing path is released: Callers must re-sync and leave edit mode.
      Parameters:
      gui - used to display prompts and errors
      showDialog - whether the user should be prompted to confirm (and possibly swap) the parent and child
      Returns:
      the outcome. A failure with no message means the operation was canceled or reported to the user

    • connectToNode

      public PathNodeEditor.Result connectToNode(Path parent, int nodeIdx, GuiUtils gui)
      Connects the active node of the editing path to a node of another path (e.g., the node snapped to by a 'magnetic' cursor). The editing path is always the child, i.e., it branches from parent. Unlike connectToSecondaryPath(GuiUtils, boolean), no confirmation is asked. On success the editing path is released: Callers must re-sync and leave edit mode.
      Parameters:
      parent - the path to branch from
      nodeIdx - the index of the node of parent to branch from
      gui - used to display errors
      Returns:
      the outcome. A failure with no message means the operation was reported to the user
      See Also:
      • canConnectTo(Path)

    • resolveNode

      public PathAndFillManager.NodeRef resolveNode(Path displayed, int index)
      Resolves a node of a displayed path to the node that connections must refer to. The paths displayed in the viewers are the versions in use: A path displayed as its fitted version is a copy that does not hold the topology, so it is resolved to its un-fitted original (see PathAndFillManager.getVersionInUse(Path))
      Parameters:
      displayed - the displayed path
      index - the index of a node of displayed
      Returns:
      the equivalent node of the path holding the topology. It is the same node if displayed is not a fitted copy

    • resolvePath

      public Path resolvePath(Path displayed)
      Parameters:

      Returns:
      the path holding the topology: the un-fitted original if displayed is a fitted copy, otherwise displayed
